title: The development of human culture
competency: Explain the processes that lead to the development of culture.

keywords.def: The symbols, language, religion, beliefs, norms, values and artifacts that are part of any society.
The physical things of a culture: tools, houses, clothing, utensils, means of transport.
Also called symbolic culture: the values, beliefs, symbols and language of a society.

en.text: Culture is the symbols, language, religion, beliefs, norms, values and artifacts of a society. It develops over thousands of years as people pass on beliefs, customs, skills and languages by teaching and imitation. Material culture is things; non-material culture is values, beliefs, symbols and language.

screens.title: The coffee ceremony
screens.ask: A grandmother teaches her granddaughter the coffee ceremony. What is being passed on?
screens.after: Culture: customs, skills and values passed from one person to another by teaching and imitation.

screens.title: Culture
paras: Culture is the symbols, language, religion, beliefs, norms, values and artifacts of any society.
Cultural processes are the ways people make the world their own.
Culture has developed for thousands of years and will continue.
People learn it from others by teaching, imitation and other social transmission.

screens.title: Two parts of culture
paras: Cultural components are material and non-material.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The symbols, language, religion, beliefs, norms, values and artifacts that are part of any society.

screens.why: Things you can touch are material.
screens.clue: Can you hold it in your hands?

screens.text: Material culture refers to the values, beliefs and language of a society.
screens.why: Those are non-material culture. Material culture is tools, houses, clothing and so on.

screens.text: How do people mainly acquire culture?
opts: By teaching and imitation from others
screens.ans: By teaching and imitation from others

screens.text: A family moves from Gondar to Hawassa and learns to make a new dish from neighbours, but keeps its own language. What does this show?
opts: Culture can change through contact, while some parts are kept
screens.ans: Culture can change through contact, while some parts are kept
screens.why: Culture develops from changes in socially passed-on customs and skills. Contact brings change; other parts are kept.

test.text: The development of culture has gone on for thousands of years.
